title: For texture tilestyle="none": define a border color
body:
Current specification says to use the default object color when a texture tilestyle is none. The way it’s specified now it’s not particularly useful. Suppose we wanted to put a multi-property “sticker” on top of object’s surface. The surface itself might be textured, translucent, etc. but the specification forces us to use object’s default color in the second layer, in areas outside sticker…

We instead recommend adding a border color attribute and defining a fixed default when unspecified.

For example: When the texture is used in other than the base layer of multi-property material, the border color is #FFFFFF00, i.e. fully transparent. RGB is white in order not to modify the color in border areas when blending in multiply mode.

Adding a border_color attribute would allow us to do many things with border being transparent etc.

3D Builder will use white as border color when tilestyle="none" in the next update which is not what is defined in the current specification.

title: Barycentric triangle interpolation
body:
Feedback from HP:
•	bilinear usually applies to interpolation within a rectangle using 4 vertices
    o	https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilinear_interpolation
    o	I don’t think I’ve seen bilinear defined for 3 vertices, if you find this and it is clear and accepted, then let’s change it.  But if not, then I don’t think we should change it.
•	barycentric is the more common term for triangular interpolation (and more general interpolation cases)
    o	https://codeplea.com/triangular-interpolation (nice interactive demo)
    o	https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barycentric_coordinate_system
•	the results in both cases are linear, so for the barycentric triangle case, it is indeed very “bilinear”-like (being a plane), but with only 3 vertices and in general non-orthogonal (very much like bilinear of a parallelogram with only 3 vertices)
    o	the math makes it look more complicated than it is…
